questions.q: What was the primary method Subhas Chandra Bose believed was necessary to gain independence, contrasting with the non-violent approach?
questions.a: Bose believed that armed struggle was necessary. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing him with other leaders who strictly followed non-violence, showing they haven't distinguished between the different strategies of the freedom movement.

questions.q: Why did Subhas Chandra Bose leave the Indian National Congress in 1939?
questions.a: He resigned due to differences with Gandhi regarding the best way to achieve independence. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks he left for personal reasons, missing the fundamental ideological disagreement about the path to freedom.

questions.q: If you were a leader during WWII, why might you seek help from countries like Germany or Japan to fight against the British in India?
questions.a: You would seek help because these countries were also rivals of the British, potentially providing weapons and support for the Indian cause. A wrong answer suggests the student doesn't understand the concept of "the enemy of my enemy is my friend" in international politics.

questions.q: How did the INA represent a shift in the location of the freedom struggle?
questions.a: Unlike protests happening within India, the INA brought the struggle to international locations and used external support. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks the INA was just a local protest group, ignoring the global nature of Bose's mission.

questions.q: Was Subhas Chandra Bose's decision to leave India to form an army a betrayal of the freedom movement? Justify your stance.
questions.a: No, it was a different strategy to achieve the same goal of independence by applying pressure from outside. A wrong answer shows the student is judging the strategy by only one standard (non-violence) rather than evaluating the goal of freedom.

questions.q: If you had to name a leader who changed the way the world viewed India's fight for freedom, why would you choose Bose?
questions.a: A good answer focuses on his willingness to step outside the borders of India and create a professional army to challenge a world power. A poor answer is vague and doesn't link his actions to the global recognition of the Indian cause.
